title: Institutions have distinct roles

blocks.heading: Institutions have distinct roles
blocks.text: The syllabus groups several international development bodies, but their mandates and institutional forms differ. The World Bank and IMF are international financial institutions, UNDP a development programme and UNICEF a children’s fund; FAO and UNESCO are specialised agencies. Match the actual need and role rather than calling them interchangeable donors.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: World Bank
blocks.text: The World Bank supports development through finance, knowledge and technical assistance, including long-term projects and institutional capacity. A proposed infrastructure or service project needs feasible design and implementation; institutional support does not prove the project’s outcomes.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: IMF
blocks.text: The IMF supports monetary cooperation and economic stability through monitoring, advice, capacity development and lending for balance-of-payments difficulties. Its stabilisation role differs from simply building schools or giving unconditional grants; lending conditions and effects require case evidence.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: UNDP
blocks.text: UNDP works on development including poverty reduction, governance, resilience and environmental sustainability through partnerships and technical support. It can help strengthen capabilities and coordination; a broad mandate does not mean it performs every service itself.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: UNICEF
blocks.text: UNICEF focuses on children’s rights and well-being, including health, nutrition, education, water and protection. Child-focused assistance can link several needs, while implementation and reach still require evidence.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: FAO
blocks.text: FAO works on food security, agriculture and related knowledge and cooperation to address hunger. Agricultural advice and evidence can support suitable production, but need local access, capabilities and conditions to become useful.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: UNESCO
blocks.text: UNESCO promotes international cooperation in education, science, culture and information. Its education and heritage work differs from general lending or food-distribution functions; select the role relevant to the development question.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Assess the arrangement
blocks.text: A fictional programme seeking child-focused nutrition support needs a different institutional role from one seeking finance for an external-payment shortfall. Match the agency’s mandate and type of assistance to the actual problem before evaluating terms and delivery. A broad international role does not mean an organisation performs every service or supplies unconditional funds.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Official mandate references
blocks.text: Roles checked 20 October 2026 against [World Bank/IMF](https://www.worldbank.org/en/about/history/the-world-bank-group-and-the-imf), [UNDP](https://www.undp.org/about-us), [UNICEF](https://www.unicef.org/what-we-do), [FAO](https://www.fao.org/about/about-fao/en/) and [UNESCO](https://www.unesco.org/en/about-us). These support the broad distinctions, not promises of a particular grant or programme outcome.
